newsitem.title: FRANCE: June rain hurt soft wheat yields in north France.
newsitem.headline: June rain hurt soft wheat yields in north France.

text.p: Farmers plan to start harvesting soft wheat at the end of the month in the Picardie region in northern France but crop officials predict that rain in June hit local yields.
High moisture levels sparked an outbreak of disease, notably fungus, and this could reduce yields, they said.
"...at this stage it does not look as good as last year because last year we had no diseases," an analyst for the local ONIC grain office in Amiens said.
Local ONIC officials forecast that soft wheat yields in France's third largest production region could drop to 8.2-8.3 tonnes from 9.0 tonnes last year.
Rain in early July last year followed by warm and dry weather helped push yields there to record levels of 10 tonnes per hectare in some fields.
But the analyst said the new estimate must be treated with caution as the first cuts would be crucial to measuring the extent of the damage.

At this stage an estimated 3-4 percent rise in area was unlikely to offset the decline in yields and the Picardie region could produce less than the 4.2 million tonnes of wheat it harvested last year.
